newsitem.title: THAILAND: Firms delay listings on depressed Thai bourse.
newsitem.headline: Firms delay listings on depressed Thai bourse.

text.p: Dozens of companies have delayed plans to list on the depressed Thai stock exchange and are expected to do so only when the bourse turns bullish again, market analysts said on Tuesday.
Unfavourable market conditions caused by investor worries about local political and economic problems have kept them from listing their firms, said Dusanee Klewpatinontha of Nithipat Capital.
The SET index has fallen 14.47 percent since the end of December until Monday, Dusanee told Reuters.
"The market is illiquid and lacks strong, good fundamentals at the moment," she added.
Locals and foreigners have been sidelined because of these negative factors, other analysts said.
They expect depressed Thai stocks to stagnate until an opposition no-confidence motion against Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa is voted on next month in parliament.
Debate on the motion, accusing Banharn of mismanagement and inefficiency, is set to start on September 18.
But the gloom overhanging the market is expected to clear after the parliamentary debate is over and whichever way the voting goes, they said.
The market hit its lowest level for this year on July 31 when the Stock Exchange of Thailand (SET) index dived to 1,064.04 points.
Another factor affecting the market is a perception among foreigners that the government may be unable to handle the slowing economy well, analysts said.
